content: The cradle, constructed from 3-cm-thick Plexiglas, is designed to securely hold the assembled test system in place, ensuring it remains steady and parallel to the bench during assays. Opaque felt pieces, not shown in the diagram, are wrapped around the clear cylinder and the rectangular port in the end caps using Velcro attachments. The spatial repellency assay system consists of the following components: 1. A treatment cylinder made of metal. 2. A clear Plexiglas cylinder equipped with a mosquito introduction portal. 3. End caps with Velcro attachments to secure felt covers. 4. Gated funnels with butterfly valves. 5. A metal spool. 6. Treatment filter paper. 7. A magnetic strip. 8. A cradle to stabilize the system. This system was adapted from Grieco JP et al.'s study, which introduced a novel high-throughput screening system to evaluate the behavioral responses of adult mosquitoes to chemicals, as published in the Journal of the American Mosquito Control Association in 2005 (Volume 21, Issue 4, Pages 404–411). Grey arrows in the schematic indicate the expected directional movement of mosquitoes during evaluations. The Y-tube olfactometer, made of acrylic, is constructed with specific components: A 32-cm acrylic wall (US Plastics part 44590) cemented onto the Y-tube base leg. A 26-cm outer diameter acrylic tube. A 0.95-cm diameter aluminum rod (Grainger part 6ALN0), which is attached to a screened circle functioning as a door. This door opens and closes to allow mosquitoes to pass during tests. A cork is used to seal the mosquito loading hole. The trapping ports are attached to the Y-tube body, with doors positioned on the sides that close tightly against the Y-tube. The end caps include a 0.8-cm collar at their base to allow for the placement of treatments and controls (e.g., delivered via vial caps) on stands inside each end cap. The end caps are then attached to the traps. One end cap lacks a screen on the side that closes against the trap, where mosquitoes are held before the experiment. A 6.5-cm gas nozzle (US Plastics part 64198) is screwed into the center of the end cap, and a 3.2-cm vacuum line (US Plastics part 57111) is connected to the nozzle. The airflow should be maintained at 0.05 m/s. An example study design for assessing attraction or inhibition of an active ingredient (AI) using the Y-tube olfactometer includes various test conditions. These conditions involve randomized treatment orders and controls, such as diluents (C0) or hand odors (H), with different concentrations of the AI (C1–C5). The informed consent form for participants in human landing catch studies includes two parts: 1. An information sheet that explains the research purpose, procedures, risks, and benefits in clear, layman’s terms. 2. A certificate of consent, where participants confirm their voluntary agreement to participate. Participants are informed that they can withdraw from the study at any time without explanation. Participants are reimbursed for their time and effort, and all costs related to the study are covered. The consent process includes opportunities for participants to ask questions and confirm their understanding of the study. If participants are illiterate, a literate witness must sign the consent form, and the participant may provide a thumbprint. A copy of the consent form is provided to each participant.
